subject: Clearhaven security questionnaire: data residency & retention (hosted API)
messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@clearhaven.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Ortega <sam.ortega@clearhaven.com>
Date: 2029-05-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on hosted API data residency + retention

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Our security team asked me to follow up with a few concrete items for our questionnaire around data residency and deletion timelines for Redwood's hosted API. High level asks:

- Where is customer data (request payloads and generated outputs) stored geographically by default?
- What are the retention windows for: (a) request/response logs, (b) cached KV/prefix caches, (c) backups/snapshots?
- When a tenant requests a full data erasure, what are the end-to-end timelines including backups?
- Do you provide evidence artifacts (audit logs, deletion attestations) we can attach to our compliance package?

We captured these as numbered items in our questionnaire (attached) — can you reply with short, actionable answers we can paste into the doc?

Appreciate it,
Lisa
Security Analyst
Clearhaven Financial

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@clearhaven.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on hosted API data residency + retention

Hi Lisa — thanks for the list. Below are concise responses you can paste into the questionnaire; I attached a one-page retention matrix and an evidence bundle with sample audit extracts. If you want us to paste these directly into the PDF, happy to do that.

1) Where data lives by default
- Hosted API request payloads and generated outputs are processed in the region of the serving endpoint you select when creating the API key. Default region is us-west-2 for accounts created in the US. We do not replicate customer request/response payloads outside the selected region for active serving.

2) Retention windows (short answers)
- Request/response logs: default retention 30 days; configurable to 7–90 days via Console.
- KV/prefix cache (ephemeral): cached entries retained up to 24 hours by default; cache TTLs are workload-configurable and can be set to 0 (no cache) for sensitive workloads.
- Backups/snapshots: encrypted daily snapshots retained 90 days by default for operational continuity; this is configurable for Dedicated/Private customers.

3) Tenant-initiated erasure timelines
- API layer: on receipt of a verified erasure request we remove live request/response artifacts within 48 hours.
- Caches: cache invalidation occurs immediately; dependent replicas are purged asynchronously (typically within 2 hours).
- Backups/snapshots: backups are removed at the next snapshot cycle and deleted from retention stores — final deletion from backup storage can take up to 30 days depending on replication lifecycles.
- We provide a deletion attestation when the process completes.

4) Evidence artifacts
- We can provide audit logs, deletion attestations, and sample backup-deletion proof (signed manifest). See attachments.

Attachments: redwood-retention-matrix.pdf (one-pager), hostedapi-evidence-bundle.zip (sample logs + manifests)

Next steps: If you need tighter retention (e.g., <30-day logs or backup retention <90 days), we can propose a contract addendum. If any question needs a fuller technical write-up I can loop in Jonas for the backup specifics.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on hosted API data residency + retention

Lisa — a couple of clarifications from the infra side that customers often ask for; feel free to paste these as supplemental notes:

- Backups: daily snapshots are region-bound and encrypted with customer-specific keys (KMS). For hosted accounts we retain snapshots in the same region by default; cross-region replication is opt-in.
- Final deletion: when we remove a backup from storage we mark the object for deletion; underlying object stores enforce eventual deletion windows depending on provider (up to 30 days). We provide the manifest with delete timestamps as evidence.
- Ephemeral caches: these are not persisted to cold storage. In rare failover scenarios we may capture cache state in transient debug bundles — these are never retained beyond incident diagnostics unless specifically requested.

I attached a small diagram showing the backup lifecycle and the deletion flow.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samuel Ortega <sam.ortega@clearhaven.com>

Date: 2029-05-02T14:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on hosted API data residency + retention

Thanks Naomi and Kimberly — this looks good and addresses most items. Two quick follow-ups from our compliance checklist:

1) Can you confirm whether request/response logs used for model quality monitoring (anonymized telemetry) ever include identifiable PII? We need an explicit statement that you either strip PII before using logs for quality work or that you only use hashed/derived identifiers.
2) For the deletion attestation: what format do you provide and is it digitally signed? Our auditor prefers a signed JSON manifest that includes object ids + deletion timestamps.

If you can confirm those two points we should be able to finalize the questionnaire.

Sam
Senior Compliance Manager
Clearhaven Financial

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortega <sam.ortega@clearhaven.com>, Lisa Park <lisa.park@clearhaven.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-03T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on hosted API data residency + retention

Hi Sam — quick answers to your two items below (paste-ready):

1) PII and monitoring telemetry
- We treat request/response logs as potential PII carriers. Before logs are used for any human review or model-quality processes, PII is either removed or obfuscated. For automated telemetry (aggregates/metrics) we only persist hashed identifiers; human-facing artifacts have PII redacted unless a customer explicitly enables identifiable debugging and signs an exception.

2) Deletion attestation format
- We provide a digitally signed JSON manifest (RSA SHA256) that lists object IDs, bucket/region, and UTC deletion timestamps. The manifest includes a signature and a Redwoods-issued certificate chain. Sample manifest included in hostedapi-evidence-bundle.zip.

Let me know if you'd like the signed manifest delivered directly to your auditors (we can set an SFTP drop or share via a signed Drive link). Happy to book a 20-minute call if the auditor wants to walk through one sample attestation.

Thanks — Naomi
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
